Nothing's on production yet." Every mix is an assumed scenario: contracts settle on it, flagged as assumed. A listed contract freezes its mold; changes apply from the next listing.
decisions: BATX gets its own three-channel mold with battery sentences (the user, 2026-10-29: battery pricing also has different agreement types), in place of the brief's section 10 open item.

Fixed-mix settlement (the user, 2026-10-29: "NO WE DONT WANT THAT. SPOT LTA AND CONTRACT NEED TO BE WEIGHTED AGAINST EACHOTHER."): every listed RAMX, NANDX and BATX contract settles on each item's fixed-mix procurement reference, its spot, contract and LTA channels weighted against each other by the item's mix, assumed or matched. This supersedes the brief's Stage 1 (the Contract channel alone) and its rule that nothing settles on an assumed scenario.

Slim sentences (the user, 2026-10-29, agreeing that bracketed terms per product are too much listing work: "agreed just have challenges deal w some of that stuff"): each sentence keeps only what defines its channel: currency and unit, product, the channel definition and the observation period; LTA keeps an agreement of at least a year with committed volume, the price in effect, its next reset and any band, and BATX's LTA its index-linked formula. Lot size, delivery days, delivery basis, volume tier and payment terms are dropped: each source settles on its own change from its own opening, so a basis it keeps constant cancels out.

Quarterly contracts with a per-quarter mix (the user, 2026-10-29: "LTA %ages of weight need to adjust dynamically depending on the Q." and "after the november 1st expiry market i want it to work in Quarters. so Q1 Q2 etc."): each item carries a mixSchedule, one mix per calendar quarter; a contract freezes its quarter's mix at listing (the quarter holding its expiry's last second; before the first scheduled quarter the first applies, after the last the last), and its listing terms document carries that mix and its commitment. The item's mixBps is the board's default and display mix, equal to the first scheduled quarter's.
Placeholders: the terms, the observation periods and the mixes are the implementing agent's reading of how these markets trade (2026-10-29), for dev; each mix is labeled an assumed scenario.
classificationNone: A purchase that fits none of the channels (unterminated quotes, resales without terms) is eligible nowhere.
componentOrder: Item-major in the basket's order, then spot, contract, lta: component index = item index * 3 + channel code.
mixRule: reference = m_spot * Spot + m_contract * Contract + m_lta * LTA over the channels' settled changes on the contract's base (the mix-weighted channel changes). Each channel enters at its own settlement: its weighted median on live data, or its degraded path's last valid value (its change at the freeze, else the listing value 0), so a failing channel keeps its fixed share; missing weight is never redistributed and the mix never shifts. Listing needs min_live_sources independent origins on every channel the mix weights. Unavailable only when the basis is none or the mix does not sum to 10,000, which no fixed-mix listing accepts; flagged when assumed.

challengeReasons.meaning: The value or the evidence is wrong, or another ground.
The purchase classifies in another channel, or in none.
The evidence traces to an earlier live source's origin, which the claim did not declare.
An LTA price carried past its own next reset.

challengeRule: Reason codes label the existing challenge: same bond, same resolution, same slash as any claim challenge.
evidenceRules: Origins, not pages. Sources whose evidence traces to the same underlying report are one origin. A source republishing another live source's origin is challengeable as a duplicate, carries no weight toward min_live_sources, and earns no delegator share.
Effective vs expired. An old publication documenting a price still in effect is valid LTA evidence. An observation carried past its reset is expired and is a false claim. The bundle must show which.

Checked at listing and at freeze. Origin count and target match are verified when a contract lists and again when it freezes. A channel that passed at listing and fails at freeze goes to the degraded path; it does not settle on stale sources.
mechanismClaim: Demonstrably off-target submissions are challengeable and slashable. This sorts what surfaces; it does not guarantee that private LTA evidence will surface.
originRule: A claim's originId is SHA-256 of "amoeba-oracle-origin-v1\n" + publisher + "\n" + report, each trimmed, ASCII-lowercased and with runs of whitespace made one space. The publisher is whoever first published the price, not a page repeating it; the report is the publication series (the table, assessment or price list), not one of its rows. The first live source of an origin in a component carries it; a later one with the same origin carries no weight, does not count toward min_live_sources and earns no delegator share.
ltaTermsRule: An LTA claim carries effectiveFrom, nextReset, floor and ceiling (unix seconds and the value's scale; 0 = none). A print is a current level at time t when effectiveFrom <= t and (nextReset = 0 or t < nextReset); past its own next reset it is no level.

classificationExamples.case: A newly signed three-year DDR5 supply agreement with committed volume; first deliveries this month.
A quarterly price reset under an LTA signed two years ago.
A memory maker and a PC OEM agree this month's contract price; delivered this month.
A distributor sells a 2,000-chip lot from stock.
A one-year frame agreement without committed volume; this quarter's price negotiated with an ODM and delivered in the quarter.
A negotiated OEM purchase delivered after the observation period, not from stock.
BATX: a five-year cell supply agreement between a cell maker and an automaker, price indexed to lithium carbonate and reset monthly.
BATX: an energy-storage integrator's tender award to a cell maker for one project, delivered this quarter.
BATX: a trader's 2 MWh of LFP cells in stock, shipped within a week.
BATX: a resale of cells of unknown origin with no stated terms.
